docs.title: Welcome to KuroAI
docs.text: KuroAI is an enterprise-grade, multi-agent generative AI pipeline and microservices engine designed for autonomous narrative parsing, structured storytelling, and scalable AI generation.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Layered Architecture: Strict dependency separation (Contracts → Engine → Agents → Inference).
  • Frozen Public APIs: Immutable API signatures guaranteed across v1.x releases.
  • Observability & Telemetry: Distributed tracing, Prometheus metrics, structured event auditing.
  • Resilience: Circuit breakers, retry policies with jitter, recovery manager, dead-letter queues.
  • Security Guardrails: Prompt safety validation, path traversal prevention, secret redaction.
  • Multi-OS CI/CD: Matrix testing on Linux (Ubuntu), Windows, and macOS.

docs.title: Project Status
docs.text:
• Current Version: 1.0.0-rc3
  • Architecture Status: Frozen (v1.0)

docs.title: Creating Custom Agents
docs.text: Agents in KuroAI process tasks and generate artifacts within the pipeline.

docs.title: Basic Structure
docs.text:
from backend.contracts.task import Task
from backend.contracts.artifact import Artifact
from backend.engine.context_engine import ContextEngine

class CustomAgent:
    def __init__(self, name: str = "CustomAgent"):
        self.name = name

    def execute_task(self, task: Task, context_engine: ContextEngine) -> Artifact:
        context = context_engine.build_context(task.id)
        # Execute agent logic using context
        return Artifact(id="art_1", artifact_type="CUSTOM_OUTPUT", content="...")

docs.title: Creating Contracts
docs.text:
Contracts reside in backend/contracts and define immutable Pydantic models.

Rules: 1. May NOT import from engine/, agents/, or inference/. 2. Must inherit from Pydantic BaseModel.

docs.title: Creating Inference Providers
docs.text:
Inference Providers encapsulate calls to LLMs and Image Generation APIs.

class CustomLLMProvider:
    def generate(self, prompt: str, **kwargs) -> str:
        # Connect to provider API and return completion
        return "Generated response"

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text: KuroAI supports three deployment configurations via Docker Compose.

docs.title: 1. Development (docker-compose.dev.yml)
docs.text:
Hot reload enabled for rapid iteration:

docker-compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build

docs.title: 2. Production (docker-compose.prod.yml)
docs.text:
Multi-worker Uvicorn server running as a non-root user:

docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

docs.title: 3. GPU Acceleration (docker-compose.gpu.yml)
docs.text:
Passes host NVIDIA GPU to container for local model inference:

docker-compose -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up -d

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12
  • Git
  • Docker (optional for containerized deployment)

docs.title: 1. Quick Developer Setup (One Command)
docs.text:
Clone the repository and run the developer bootstrap script:

git clone https://github.com/Sachin-pandey13/KuroAI.git
cd KuroAI
python scripts/bootstrap.py

This will automatically: 1. Verify Python version 2. Install developer dependencies (requirements/dev.txt) 3. Setup pre-commit git hooks 4. Run the Architecture Validator

docs.title: 2. Manual Installation
docs.text:
# Core server runtime only:
pip install -r requirements/runtime.txt

# Full developer suite:
pip install -r requirements/dev.txt

# Heavy ML dependencies (for local generation):
pip install -r requirements/ml.txt

docs.title: 3. Running the Server locally
docs.text:
uvicorn backend.api.app:app --reload --port 8000

Check health endpoints: - Liveness: http://localhost:8000/health/liveness - Readiness: http://localhost:8000/health/readiness - Metrics: http://localhost:8000/metrics

docs.title: Plugin Guide
docs.text: KuroAI supports plugins via custom agents, tools, and inference adapters registered dynamically with CapabilityRegistry.

docs.title: Testing Guide
docs.text:
KuroAI includes unit, security, resilience, and stress test suites.

# Unit tests
pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/stress

# Security tests
pytest tests/test_security.py -v

# Resilience tests
pytest tests/test_resilience.py -v

# Stress tests
pytest tests/stress/ -v

# Benchmarks
python -m benchmarks.runner

docs.title: Semantic Versioning Policy
docs.text:
KuroAI strictly adheres to Semantic Versioning 2.0.0.

Format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE]

docs.title: 1. MAJOR Version (X.0.0)
docs.text: Incurred when breaking changes are introduced to public API signatures or architectural laws. - Changing AgentRuntime.run_task() or ContextEngine.build_context() signatures. - Modifying backend.contracts Pydantic model contracts in a non-backward-compatible manner.

docs.title: 2. MINOR Version (1.X.0)
docs.text: Incurred when new capabilities or features are added in a backward-compatible manner. - Adding a new Agent type or Inference Provider. - Adding new public engine utility methods without breaking existing signatures.

docs.title: 3. PATCH Version (1.0.X)
docs.text: Incurred for backward-compatible bug fixes and performance optimizations. - Fixing internal engine bugs or edge-case handling. - Documentation updates or CI pipeline refinements.

docs.title: 4. Release Candidates (1.0.0-rcN)
docs.text: Release candidates represent stabilization and hardening phases before a major/minor release. - rc1: Architecture freeze - rc2: Production hardening (telemetry, security, resilience) - rc3: Open-source repository engineering & DX

docs.title: ADR-001 — Event Bus Architecture
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-02 Status: Accepted Authors: KuroAI Architecture Team

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
KuroAI's subsystems need to communicate state changes without creating tight coupling. For example:

  • When ArtifactRegistry registers an artifact, ProjectStateEngine should initialize status.
  • When AgentRuntime completes a task, TaskRegistry should update task status.
  • When ProjectStateEngine transitions state, downstream observers may need to react.

The naive approach — direct method calls between subsystems — creates a dense dependency web that contradicts the single-responsibility principle and makes the system hard to test in isolation.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We use an in-process synchronous EventBus as the primary decoupling mechanism between blackboard subsystems.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
class EventBus:
    def subscribe(self, event_type: str, handler: Callable) -> None
    def publish(self, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None
    def unsubscribe(self, event_type: str, handler: Callable) -> None
  • Synchronous dispatch: handlers are called inline during publish().
  • No persistence: events are ephemeral; not stored.
  • String-typed events: event types are plain strings (e.g., "artifact.registered", "task.completed").

docs.title: Event Type Conventions
docs.text:
<domain>.<verb>

artifact.registered
artifact.updated
task.registered
task.status_updated
task.completed
agent.started
agent.completed
state.transitioned

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - Subsystems do not import each other; they only import EventBus. - Each subsystem can be unit-tested by asserting published events. - Adding new cross-subsystem behaviors requires only a new subscriber.

Negative: - Synchronous dispatch means a slow handler blocks the publisher. - Event ordering is implicit (subscription order). - No replay or persistence for debugging.

Mitigations: - Handlers must be fast (no I/O, no LLM calls). - Future RC may introduce async dispatch as an opt-in via a wrapper.

docs.title: ADR-002 — Context Engine Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-02 Status: Accepted Authors: KuroAI Architecture Team

docs.title: Context
docs.text: KuroAI's agents need rich context to make decisions: what artifacts exist, what their current state is, what depends on what, and what version is current. Without a structured assembly process, each agent would independently query the blackboard — duplicating logic and creating implicit coupling to the engine layer.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We introduce ContextEngine as the single entry point for assembling a ContextBundle before any agent execution.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
class ContextEngine:
    def assemble_context(self, task: Task) -> ContextBundle
    def register_section_provider(self, selector: ContextSelector, retriever: BaseRetriever) -> None
  • assemble_context() queries ArtifactRegistry, DependencyGraph, VersionGraph and merges results into a single ContextBundle.
  • register_section_provider() allows extending the context with domain-specific retrievers (e.g., a retriever that adds screenplay formatting rules to context for screenplay agents).
  • ContextBundle is a frozen Pydantic model — immutable once assembled.
  • ContextSelector is an enum — guards against typo-based bugs in provider registration.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
Task → ContextEngine.assemble_context()
    → BaseRetriever(s) per ContextSelector
    → ContextBundle (immutable)
    → Agent.execute(context_bundle)

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - Agents are decoupled from all blackboard subsystems — they only receive a ContextBundle. - Context assembly is testable in isolation. - New context sections can be added without modifying any agent.

Negative: - ContextEngine accumulates dependencies on multiple engine subsystems. - Context is assembled on every task — no caching. (Intentional for RC-1 correctness.)

Future: - RC-2 may introduce selective context assembly (only fetch sections relevant to the agent's agent_type). - Caching of unchanged context sections may be introduced with a hash-based invalidation strategy.

docs.title: ADR-003 — Agent Runtime Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-02 Status: Accepted Authors: KuroAI Architecture Team

docs.title: Context
docs.text: KuroAI needs a single orchestration point that takes a Task, routes it to the correct agent, provides it with context, executes it, and records the result. Without a centralized runtime, this logic would be scattered across pipeline scripts, orchestrators, and individual agents.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: AgentRuntime is the single pipeline executor. It is the only class that should coordinate between the engine layer and the agent layer.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
class AgentRuntime:
    async def run_task(self, task: Task) -> AgentResult
    async def execute_task(self, task: Task) -> AgentResult   # alias
    def register_agent(self, agent: BaseAgent) -> None
    def get_agent(self, agent_type: str) -> BaseAgent

docs.title: Execution Pipeline
docs.text:
run_task(task)
    1. task_registry.update_status(task.task_id, RUNNING)
    2. event_bus.publish("task.started", {...})
    3. context = context_engine.assemble_context(task)
    4. agent = agent_registry.get_agent(task.agent_type)
    5. result = await agent.execute(task, context)
    6. artifact_registry.update(result.artifact) if result.artifact
    7. state_engine.transition(artifact_id, new_status)
    8. task_registry.update_status(task.task_id, COMPLETED)
    9. event_bus.publish("task.completed", {...})
    10. return result

docs.title: Separation of Concerns
docs.text:
Concern Owner Task routing AgentRuntime Agent storage AgentRegistry Context assembly ContextEngine Tool execution CapabilityRegistry State transitions ProjectStateEngine Event notifications EventBus

AgentRuntime coordinates, it does not implement any of the above directly.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - One place to add cross-cutting concerns (logging, metrics, retry, human review). - Agents are pure: they receive (task, context) and return AgentResult. - Pipeline is fully observable via EventBus events.

Negative: - AgentRuntime depends on all blackboard subsystems — it is inherently high-coupling. - This is acceptable because AgentRuntime is the orchestration boundary, not a domain class.

Mitigations: - All subsystem dependencies are injected via constructor — no service locator, no globals. - AgentRuntime itself is unit-testable with mocked dependencies.

docs.title: ADR-004 — Human Review Integration
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-02 Status: Proposed (RC-2 scope) Authors: KuroAI Architecture Team

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
KuroAI is a generative AI pipeline that produces creative artifacts (story plans, scenes, images). Some output may require human review before proceeding to downstream steps. Without a structured review gate, either:

  1. All output proceeds automatically (risk of cascading bad generations), or
  2. All output pauses for manual intervention (blocks automation).

A structured human review mechanism allows selective, policy-driven review gates.

docs.title: Decision (Proposed for RC-2)
docs.text: Introduce a HumanReviewGate as a first-class subsystem alongside AgentRuntime.

docs.title: Design (Proposed)
docs.text:
class HumanReviewGate:
    def requires_review(self, artifact: Artifact, policy: ReviewPolicy) -> bool
    async def request_review(self, artifact: Artifact) -> ReviewDecision
    def auto_approve(self, artifact: Artifact) -> ReviewDecision

ReviewDecision is an enum: APPROVED, REJECTED, REVISION_REQUESTED.

docs.title: Integration Point
docs.text:
AgentRuntime.run_task() will check HumanReviewGate.requires_review() after agent.execute() and before artifact_registry.update():

... agent.execute(task, context) → AgentResult
    → if review_gate.requires_review(result.artifact, policy):
        → decision = await review_gate.request_review(result.artifact)
        → if decision == REJECTED: raise AgentRuntimeError
        → if decision == REVISION_REQUESTED: re-queue task
    → artifact_registry.update(result.artifact)

docs.title: Review Policies
docs.text:
class ReviewPolicy(Enum):
    NEVER = "never"           # fully automated
    ALWAYS = "always"         # always require review
    ON_CONFIDENCE_LOW = "on_confidence_low"   # review if agent confidence < threshold
    ON_FIRST_DRAFT = "on_first_draft"         # review only version 1 of each artifact

docs.title: Status: RC-1 Stub
docs.text:
For RC-1, HumanReviewGate is not implemented. The AgentRuntime has a placeholder _human_review attribute set to None, which future RC-2 work can populate.

The architecture is designed so that inserting the gate requires modifying only AgentRuntime.run_task() — no other classes need to change.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - Human review is a first-class concept, not bolted on later. - Policies make review behavior explicit and configurable. - Selective review avoids blocking the entire pipeline.

Negative: - Async review introduces latency in the pipeline. - RC-2 must design the notification/callback mechanism (WebSocket? polling?).

Open Questions (for RC-2): 1. How does a human reviewer submit a decision? (API endpoint? CLI? Web UI?) 2. How long should the system wait before auto-approving (timeout policy)? 3. Should rejected artifacts be automatically re-queued or require manual restart?

docs.title: Preamble
docs.text: KuroAI 2.0 is an Autonomous AI Manga Studio powered by a team of stateless, specialized AI agents collaborating with the user (Human Creative Director) via a shared, event-driven Project State Engine (Blackboard Architecture).

docs.title: Section I: The Six Laws of KuroAI
First Law (Incremental Preservation)
docs.text: The system must never force the user to restart creative work because of a later modification. If a user changes a single detail (e.g., hairstyle, camera angle, dialogue line), the system shall evaluate the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of node dependencies, selectively invalidate only affected downstream artifacts, and preserve everything else.

docs.title: Second Law (Transparency & Reproducibility)
docs.text: Every AI decision must be transparent, explainable, and 100% reproducible. Every artifact generated by an agent must include a structured DecisionTrace containing confidence score, reasoning rationale, identified risks, evaluated alternatives, and exact execution provenance (prompts, seeds, model identifiers, LoRAs, ControlNets, samplers, hyper-parameters).

docs.title: Third Law (Editability & Reversibility)
docs.text: Every creative artifact must be editable and reversible. Edits shall be non-destructive and tracked at the node level within the VersionGraph. Users can view, roll back, branch, or manually override any artifact at any point in history.

docs.title: Fourth Law (State Single Source of Truth)
docs.text: The Project State Engine (Blackboard) is the sole owner and single source of truth for all project data. Agents are strictly stateless transformers that accept context inputs and output state deltas, events, and decision traces. Agents shall never persist or own project state locally.

docs.title: Fifth Law (Single Responsibility & Decoupling)
docs.text: Every agent must specialize in a single domain of expertise and collaborate exclusively via shared state events published to the Project State Engine. Direct inter-agent invocation or coupling is strictly prohibited.

docs.title: Sixth Law (Human Final Authority)
docs.text: Human creativity has absolute, final authority over AI autonomy. The user directs the vision, sets goal constraints, overrides AI proposals, and selects working autonomy levels (Guided Mode, Smart Mode, Autonomous Studio Mode).

docs.title: Section II: Master System Architecture
docs.text:
Human Creative Director
                          │
                          ▼
                Project Manager Agent
                          │
                          ▼
                  Publish Creative Goal
                          │
                          ▼
                Project State Engine
                  (Blackboard Core)
                          │
      ┌──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
      ▼              ▼              ▼              ▼
 Dependency Graph  Version Graph  Event Bus   Artifact Registry
 (Node-Level DAG) (Node History) (Abstract)   (UUID, Version)
      │              │              │              │
      └──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
                   Context Engine
                 (Context Policies)
                          │
                          ▼
                     Task Scheduler
                          │
          ┌───────────────┼────────────────┐
          ▼               ▼                ▼
     Story Agent    Character Agent   Image Agent
     (BaseAgent)      (BaseAgent)     (BaseAgent)
          │               │                │
          └───────────────┼────────────────┘
                          ▼
                 Capability Registry
                          │
                      Capability (e.g. GenerateImage)
                          │
                      Provider (ComfyUI / Replicate / Local SD)
                          │
                        Model (Flux / SDXL / Gemini)

docs.title: Section III: Engineering Standards
docs.text:
1. Contract-First Architecture: No engine or agent code shall be written without first defining and freezing its contract schema in backend/contracts/.
  2. Type Safety & Pydantic v2: All contracts use strict Python type annotations and Pydantic v2 models.
  3. Usable Milestones: Development proceeds in isolated, fully verified milestones (Contracts & Skeleton $\rightarrow$ State Engine $\rightarrow$ Dependency Graph $\rightarrow$ Event Bus $\rightarrow$ Scheduler $\rightarrow$ Capabilities $\rightarrow$ Agents $\rightarrow$ Integration).
  4. Single Responsibility: Every module has a single, well-defined contract. No feature bleed across phases.
